title: Minimum Replacements to Sort the Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to sort the array in non-decreasing order.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to sort the array in non-decreasing order. An operation consists of replacing any element with two elements that sum to it.
constraints: One operation splits one value into two positive values with the same sum; repeat as needed.
Minimize operations so the resulting sequence is nondecreasing.
hints: Work right-to-left with the maximum value the current element’s parts may have.
Use the fewest parts whose ceiling size is at most that maximum.
parts=ceil(value/maximum); add parts-1 operations; the smallest resulting part value//parts becomes the new bound.
Balanced parts maximize the smallest part for a fixed count, preserving the loosest possible bound for earlier elements, so the greedy choice cannot hurt the prefix.
editorial: Balanced parts maximize the smallest part for a fixed count, preserving the loosest possible bound for earlier elements, so the greedy choice cannot hurt the prefix.

tests.explanation: Split nine into three equal parts using two operations, yielding all threes.
The input is already nondecreasing, so no split is needed.
